Copper-catalyzed 1,4-alkylcyanation of
CF3-containing 1,3-enynes: alkoxy radical-mediated
selective cleavage of fused azabicycles
Jun-Lin Lu, Hong-Fei Liu, Ying-Xin Shui, Qi-Chao Shan, Xin-Hua Duan
 * and
Li-Na Guo
 *
A copper-catalyzed 1,4-alkylcyanation of CF3-containing 1,3-enynes
with bicyclic hydroperoxides and TMSCN is described. In this cascade,
the alkyl source originates from selective cleavage of a C–C bond in
the fused bicyclic skeletons, enabling the successful introduction of a
succinimide fragment into tetrasubstituted allenes. This reaction is
characterized by mild conditions, broad substrate scope, excellent
functional group tolerance, and ease of large-scale synthesis and
product derivatization.
In recent years, radical-mediated C–C bond cleavage of un-
strained aliphatic carbocycles has emerged as a powerful plat-
form for the formation of various chemical bonds. Significant
progress has been made in the alkoxy-radical mediated ring-
opening of monocarbocycles, which enables the successful
introduction of ketoalkyl fragments into various compounds.
1
In contrast, the alkoxy radical-induced C–C bond cleavage of
fused bicyclic skeletons remains less developed, even though
there were pioneering reports in the 1980s (Scheme 1a). 2
In particular, the selective cleavage of fused bicyclic skeletons
remains a significant yet relatively less explored area. Recently,
Zuo’s group reported an elegant photoinduced Ce-catalyzed
aerobic oxidative ring expansion of hemiketal alcohols (tauto-
mer mixture) to carbonyl-containing macrolatones via a ligand-
to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) strategy.
3 Our group has
developed several abundant metal-catalyzed ring expansion/
cross-coupling cascades of hemiketal hydroperoxides, yielding
a range of site-specific functionalized macrolactones.
4 Remark-
ably, by adjusting the substituents on the bicyclic skeletons, 5a
we achieved an unexpected Cu-catalyzed ring-opening/amino-
carbonylation cascade, yielding amides that contain a g-lactam
or succinimide fragment instead (Scheme 1b).
5b DFT calcula-
tions revealed that the regioselective ring-opening is thermo-
dynamically and kinetically favorable, due to the formation of a
stable g-lactam or succinimide fragment and an unstrained
alkyl radical. These intriguing findings motivated us to explore
new radical alkylation reactions, with the aim of incorporating
these functionalized alkyl moieties into diverse molecules.
Radical-mediated multicomponent reactions represent an
eﬃcient strategy for the rapid assembly of complex molecules
from simple starting materials, characterized by mild reaction
conditions, high step-economy and superior bond formation
eﬃciency. In this field, 1,3-enynes have been extensively used
as versatile linkage bridges.
6 A variety of three-component
functionalization reactions of 1,3-enynes have been developed
including 1,2-functionalization,
7 1,4-functionalization,8 and
3,4-functionalization.9 Among these, the radical-mediated 1,4-
difunctionalization of 1,3-enynes has gradually emerged as an
important and powerful strategy for the synthesis of poly-
substituted allenes.
10 In particular, the copper-catalyzed 1,4-
alkylcyanation of 1,3-enynes provides an eﬃcient method for
the rapid synthesis of CN-functionalized tetrasubstituted
allenes. A range of alkyl radical precursors, including alkyl

complex I formed in situ, yielding the radical intermediate III
and the Cu( II) species II. Subsequently, the alkoxy radical III
undergoes a selective b-scission to give the ring-opening, rela-
tively stable alkyl radical IV. Intermediate IV is captured by the
CF3-1,3-enyne 2a to form a propargyl radical species V, which
resonates to produce the allenyl radical VI. Meanwhile, the
Cu(II) species II undergoes a ligand exchange with TMSCN to
yield the key intermediate VII. The interaction of intermediates

elimination of Cu( III) species VIII gives the target product 3aa
and regenerates the Cu( I) complex I. Fortunately, all relevant
copper complexes can be detected by HRMS.
In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed 1,4-
alkylcyanation of 1,3-enynes with bicyclic hydroperoxides and
TMSCN. In this cascade, the bicyclic hydroperoxides serve as a
functionalized alkyl source via an alkoxy radical-mediated
selective b-scission, enabling the introduction of a succinimide
fragment into polysubstituted allenes. This method has signif-
icant advantages, including mild reaction conditions, excellent
functional group tolerance, and ease of large-scale synthesis
and product derivatization. Additionally, this cascade can be
extended to the 1,4-alkylazidation of 1,3-enynes. This work not
only enriches the diverse synthesis of functionalized allenes but
also provides a good example of selective C–C bond cleavage in
bicyclic skeletons.

resonates to produce the allenyl radical VI. Meanwhile, the

yield the key intermediate VII. The interaction of intermediates
VI and VII forms a Cu(III) species VIII. Finally, reductive
elimination of Cu(III) species VIII gives the target product 3aa
and regenerates the Cu(I) complex I. Fortunately, all relevant
copper complexes can be detected by HRMS.

In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed 1,4-
alkylcyanation of 1,3-enynes with bicyclic hydroperoxides and
TMSCN. In this cascade, the bicyclic hydroperoxides serve as a
functionalized alkyl source via an alkoxy radical-mediated
selective b-scission, enabling the introduction of a succinimide
fragment into polysubstituted allenes. This method has signif-
icant advantages, including mild reaction conditions, excellent
functional group tolerance, and ease of large-scale synthesis
and product derivatization. Additionally, this cascade can be
extended to the 1,4-alkylazidation of 1,3-enynes. This work not
only enriches the diverse synthesis of functionalized allenes but
also provides a good example of selective C–C bond cleavage in
bicyclic skeletons.
